question:
A 3-year-old healthy girl is brought to the emergency department due to concerns about an abdominal
mass. Her parents report a 3-week history of abdominal pain, reduced appetite, and a progressively
protuberant abdomen. This morning, while bathing her, they felt a hard area beneath her ribs. She has
not experienced weight loss, fevers, or changes in bowel habits. On examination, the child appears
playful and well. Vital signs include a heart rate of 97 beats per minute, blood pressure of 116/53 mm
Hg, respiratory rate of 15 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 100% on room air. Palpation
reveals a firm, nontender mass in the right upper quadrant extending approximately 4 cm below the
costal margin. Her abdomen is distended but soft, and the remainder of the physical examination is
unremarkable. Laboratory tests, including a complete blood count and comprehensive metabolic panel,
are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Hydatid cyst (B)
Wilms tumor (C) Hepatoblastoma (D) Mesenteric cyst (E) Polycystic kidney disease (F) Sarcoma (G)
Hepatic hemangioma (H) Teratoma (I) Rhabdomyosarcoma (J) Adrenal carcinoma
 A. Hepatoblastoma
B. Polycystic kidney disease
C. Teratoma
D. Wilms tumor
E. Hydatid cyst
F. Adrenal carcinoma
G. Mesenteric cyst
H. Sarcoma
I. Rhabdomyosarcoma
J. Hepatic hemangioma
